vulnerability_analysis: The vulnerability is a reentrancy in the swapAndLiquify function. When swapTokensForEth is called, it sends ETH to address(this), which can trigger a malicious contract's receive function. The lockTheSwap modifier only prevents reentrancy from the same function, but the receive function can call transfer again, bypassing the inSwapAndLiquify check because the transfer path goes through _transfer -> swapAndLiquify again before the first swapAndLiquify completes.
attack_strategy: Deploy a malicious contract that re-enters during the ETH transfer in swapTokensForEth. The contract will hold JizzJet tokens and trigger the initial swapAndLiquify. During the receive callback, it will call transfer again to trigger another swapAndLiquify before the first one finishes updating balances.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Deploy attacker contract with reentrant receive function. 2. Fund attacker with JizzJet tokens. 3. Trigger initial transfer to start swapAndLiquify. 4. In receive(), call transfer again to re-enter. 5. Repeat multiple times to drain ETH from swaps.
